plan.contextChunk: This figure contains two side-by-side panels illustrating 2D translation as a geometric transformation in the xy-plane. In the left panel, an orange square at the origin is displaced to an upper-right position by a translation vector t, shown as a red arrow; the transformed square sits at coordinates (t_x, t_y) relative to the original. In the right panel, two successive translations are depicted: the square first moves by vector t to an intermediate position, then by vector s to a final position, with individual red arrows labeled t and s; a third red arrow labeled t+s connects the original square directly to the final position, demonstrating that the composition of two translations equals their vector sum. This figure establishes the additive composition rule for 2D translations, motivating their representation in homogeneous coordinates where composition reduces to matrix multiplication.

interactionPlan.concept: A 2D translation displaces every point of a shape by the same vector, and composing two translations is just adding their vectors (a single translation t+s).
elements: Two side-by-side panels sharing the same scale, separated by a thin vertical divider: LEFT panel 'a single translation', RIGHT panel 'composition of two translations'

LEFT panel y-axis: vertical black arrow pointing up with italic serif 'y' at the arrowhead

RIGHT panel red arrow t: origin center to intermediate center, bold label 't'
RIGHT panel red arrow s: intermediate center to final center, bold label 's'

Compact numeric readout in the UI panel: t = (tx, ty), s = (sx, sy), t+s = (tx+sx, ty+sy)

demo_steps.title: Second translation s

interactionPlan.reconstructionNotes: Two equal-width panels filling the full canvas, divided by a thin light vertical rule; the drawing (axes, squares, arrows) occupies the entire width — no inline matrix column. Each panel has its own origin toward the lower-left with a thin black x-axis arrow right and y-axis arrow up, italic serif 'x' and 'y' at the arrowheads. Stage stepping only dims/hides elements in the RIGHT panel; the left panel always stays fully opaque. Numeric readouts live in the surrounding UI panel, and the 3x3 homogeneous matrices appear only in an overlay popup toggled from the UI, rendered at comfortably readable size with the translation column tinted red.

authoredContext:
Consider a translation by a 2D vector, $(t_x, t_y)$ as shown in
-translations. We'll denote the coordinates after the
transformation with a prime. In heterogeneous coordinates, we have
$$\begin{pmatrix}
 x' \\
 y' 
 \end{pmatrix}
 =
 \begin{pmatrix}
 x \\
 y 
 \end{pmatrix}
 +
 \begin{pmatrix}
 t_x \\
 t_y 
 \end{pmatrix}
$$

(left) Translation. (right) Composition of two consecutive translations.

In summary, in homogeneous coordinates a translation becomes a product
with a matrix, and chaining translations can be done by multiplying the
matrices together. The benefits of using the homogeneous coordinates
will become more obvious later.

When chaining rotations and translations only we will have a euclidean
transformation (lengths and angles between lines are preserved). A
similarity transform is the result of chaining a rotation,
translation and scaling (with uniform scaling, $s_x=s_y$). In this case
angles are preserved but not lengths. Chaining all transformations
results in an affine transformation. Each set of transformations
forms a group.

In general, chaining translations, scalings, rotations and shears will
result in a generic matrix with the form: $$\mathbf{p}' = 
 \begin{bmatrix}
 a & b & c \\
 d & e & f \\
 0 & 0 & 1
 \end{bmatrix}
 \mathbf{p}$$ Any transformation with that form (6 degrees of
freedom) is an affine transformation. An affine transformation has the
property that parallel lines will remain parallel after the
transformation; however, lengths and non-zero angles might change.

plan.concept: A 2D translation is a vector displacement of a shape, and composing two translations is simply adding their vectors — which in homogeneous coordinates becomes multiplying their 3×3 matrices.
elements: x-axis: horizontal black arrow pointing right, italic label 'x' near the arrowhead
y-axis: vertical black arrow pointing up, italic label 'y' near the arrowhead
Origin square: orange filled square with thick black outline, centered on the origin (axes pass through its center)
Translated square T: orange filled square with black outline, at position offset by vector t from the origin square
Translated square T+S: orange filled square with black outline, at position offset by t+s from the origin square (only in the composed view)
Red arrow t: from origin (center of origin square) to center of square T, bold label 't'
Red arrow s: from center of square T to center of square T+S, bold label 's'
Red arrow t+s: from origin directly to center of square T+S, bold label 't+s'
Draggable handles at the tips of arrows t and s (small red circles) with subtle hover highlight
Numeric readout of current components: t = (tx, ty), s = (sx, sy), t+s = (tx+sx, ty+sy)
Homogeneous matrix panel: 3×3 matrix T(t) = [[1,0,tx],[0,1,ty],[0,0,1]]
Homogeneous matrix panel: 3×3 matrix T(s) = [[1,0,sx],[0,1,sy],[0,0,1]]
Product panel: T(s)·T(t) = [[1,0,tx+sx],[0,1,ty+sy],[0,0,1]] with the sum entries highlighted
Faint dashed guide lines from each square's center down to the x-axis and across to the y-axis showing components
Ghost outline of the original square left at the origin for reference
Caption/annotation: 'composition of translations = vector addition'

interactions.teaches: The translation vector IS the displacement: moving the arrow tip moves the square rigidly, and the matrix's third column is exactly the vector components.
Translation composition builds up in stages: start at the origin, apply t, then apply s from there, and finally see that the single arrow t+s reaches the same place.
interactions.label: Composition stage

interactions.teaches: Translations commute — applying s first and then t lands the square in exactly the same final position, and the matrix product is the same either way.
interactions.label: Order of composition

demo_steps.title: The untranslated square
demo_steps.narration: An orange square sits centered on the origin of the xy-plane. Nothing has moved yet; this is the reference position the ghost outline will keep marking.

demo_steps.title: One translation t
demo_steps.narration: A red arrow t carries the square up and to the right. Drag the arrow tip: every point of the square moves by the same vector, and the homogeneous matrix T(t) changes only in its third column, (tx, ty).

demo_steps.title: A second translation s
demo_steps.narration: From the intermediate square, a second red arrow s displaces it again to the lower right. Two separate moves, two separate matrices.

demo_steps.title: The composed vector t+s
demo_steps.narration: A single arrow drawn from the origin straight to the final square closes the triangle: t+s. The matrix product T(s)·T(t) has third column (tx+sx, ty+sy) — the composition is just vector addition.

demo_steps.title: Order doesn't matter
demo_steps.narration: Swap the order to s then t: the intermediate square moves elsewhere, but the final square and the arrow t+s are unchanged. Translation matrices commute.

plan.keyInsight: Chaining translations is nothing more than adding their vectors — and homogeneous coordinates encode that addition as ordinary matrix multiplication, so translation joins rotation and scaling as a single 3×3 matrix.
plan.reconstructionNotes: Single wide panel (replacing the book's two sub-panels) with a thin black x-axis arrow pointing right and y-axis arrow pointing up, italic serif 'x' and 'y' labels at the arrowheads; origin near the lower-left. Squares are solid orange (#F5901E-ish) with thick black outlines, all the same size, about one-eighth of the panel width. The origin square straddles the origin so both axes cross its center; keep a pale dashed ghost of it once translations are applied. Vectors are thick bright red arrows with solid triangular heads and bold serif labels 't', 's', 't+s' placed just off the shaft. Typical layout: t points up-right at roughly 40°, s points down-right and shorter, so t+s is a long shallow arrow to the right — forming a clear triangle. Small red circular drag handles sit at the tips of t and s. A side panel shows the two 3×3 homogeneous matrices and their product stacked vertically, with the tx, ty and tx+sx, ty+sy entries tinted red to tie them to the arrows. Faint gray dashed drop lines from square centers to the axes show components. Keep the figure uncluttered; only the arrows active in the current stage are drawn at full opacity, earlier ones fade slightly.

Each panel has its own origin toward the lower-left with a thin black x-axis arrow right and y-axis arrow up, italic serif 'x' and 'y' at the arrowheads. Squares are solid orange (~#F5901E) with thick black outlines, all identical, roughly one-sixth of a panel's width; the origin square is centered on the origin so both axes cross it. Vectors are thick bright red arrows with solid triangular heads; labels 't', 's', 't+s' in large bold serif with a white halo, sized to stay legible when the figure is rendered at about half scale. Left panel: origin square, arrow t up-right at ~40 degrees, translated square. Right panel: origin square, arrow t to the intermediate square, shorter arrow s pointing down-right to the final square, and the long shallow arrow t+s from origin to final square forming a clear triangle. Small red circular handles at the tips of t and s. No dashed component guides, no grey caption, no extra annotation text in the drawing area. Stage stepping only dims/hides elements in the RIGHT panel; the left panel always stays fully opaque. Numeric readouts live in the surrounding UI panel, and the 3x3 homogeneous matrices appear only in an overlay popup toggled from the UI, rendered at comfortably readable size with the translation column tinted red.

discrepancies: The whole drawing is rendered small inside its container (viewBox 1160×440 scaled to ~580px), so the bold vector labels t, s, t+s and the italic x / y axis labels appear noticeably smaller and less prominent than in the source, where they are large, heavy display-weight glyphs.
Small white/red circular drag rings sit at every arrow tip; these do not exist in the source and slightly clutter the red arrowheads at inline size.
A faint vertical divider line is drawn between the two panels; the source has no such separator (barely visible, but an addition).

In the right panel of the source the 's' label sits clearly in the open space above/right of the s arrow, well clear of the intermediate square; in the render it crowds the right edge of the intermediate square box.
Stroke weights of the axes and arrows are proportionally thinner than the very heavy black/red strokes of the printed source, giving a lighter overall look.
evaluation.notes: Structurally faithful two-panel reproduction of translation composition with correct squares, red arrows, arrowheads and t / s / t+s labels, backed by an unusually rich and pedagogically apt interaction set (stage select, order swap, four component sliders, draggable tips, matrix popup, 5-step player); main weaknesses are the reduced on-screen scale making labels and strokes less prominent than the bold printed original plus minor added chrome (drag rings, divider).
action_items: Reduce the viewBox width (or increase font sizes to ~52-56 units) so the bold t, s, t+s labels and italic x/y axis labels render at the same visual prominence as the heavy display type in the source.
Thicken axis and arrow strokes (and the square outlines) proportionally so the figure reads with the same weight as the printed original at inline size.
Make the drag rings appear only on hover (opacity 0 by default) and remove the faint vertical divider so the default state is a clean drop-in replacement for the static image.
Nudge the 's' label placement search to prefer the open whitespace above/right of the s arrow, away from the intermediate square edge, matching the source layout.

feedback.rationale: Concept and interaction structure are sound; remaining issues are purely implementation details (font/stroke scale, drag-ring chrome, divider removal, label placement) best fixed in the generator.
